title: DiffVQE: Hybrid Diffusion Voice Quality Enhancement Under Acoustic Echo and Noise
summary: Acoustic echo and background noise pose challenges on speech enhancement in hands-free systems and speakerphones. Discriminatively trained end-to-end methods represent a powerful solution for joint acoustic echo control (AEC) and denoising. However, with the advent of generative methods, diffusion-based approaches have seen remarkable performance in speech enhancement tasks. In this work, to the best of our knowledge, we provide the first (still non-causal) diffusion-based AEC model (DiffVQE) that is reproducible in terms of topology, training data, and training framework. So far, without employing diffusion, Microsoft's discriminative DeepVQE model has been shown to excel any of the ICASSP 2023 AEC Challenge entries achieving remarkable performance. Using data from the Interspeech 2025 URGENT Challenge for a diverse, high-quality training dataset, our DiffVQE excels DeepVQE both in echo and noise control performance, as well as in computational complexity and model size.

AI.tldr: DiffVQE is the first reproducible diffusion-based acoustic echo control and denoising model, outperforming Microsoft's discriminative DeepVQE model in echo/noise control, computational complexity, and model size on Interspeech 2025 URGENT Challenge data.
AI.motivation: Acoustic echo and background noise degrade speech enhancement in hands-free systems and speakerphones; existing discriminative end-to-end methods (like DeepVQE) are powerful but diffusion-based approaches have shown promise yet lacked AEC applications with reproducibility.
AI.method: DiffVQE is a diffusion-based (non-causal) model for joint acoustic echo control and denoising, designed to be reproducible in topology, training data, and training framework, trained on diverse, high-quality data from the Interspeech 2025 URGENT Challenge.
AI.result: DiffVQE outperforms Microsoft's discriminative DeepVQE model in both echo and noise control performance, while also achieving lower computational complexity and smaller model size.
AI.conclusion: Diffusion-based generative methods can surpass state-of-the-art discriminative models for joint AEC and denoising, offering both better performance and greater efficiency; DiffVQE provides a reproducible baseline for future research.

title: A Stochastic Hybrid Automaton for Smartphone Battery Dynamics: Electro-Thermal Coupling and First-Passage Time-to-Empty Estimation
comment: Based on the authors' solution to Problem A of the 2026 Mathematical Contest in Modeling (MCM), awarded Finalist
summary:
Smartphone time-to-empty (TTE) is difficult to predict because shutdown is governed not only by remaining charge, but also by instantaneous power capability under temperature-, aging-, and load-dependent voltage sag. We develop a stochastic hybrid automaton for smartphone battery dynamics that couples a first-order Thevenin equivalent-circuit model with a lumped thermal model and a stochastic user-activity process. The continuous state includes state of charge, polarization voltage, and battery temperature; user behavior is represented as a piecewise deterministic Markov process switching among idle, social/web, video, gaming, and weak-signal modes. Shutdown is formulated as a first-passage event when terminal voltage crosses a cutoff threshold or when requested power exceeds the instantaneous feasibility envelope.
  The model captures a voltage-collapse mechanism that simple Coulomb-counting or linear discharge models miss: cold temperature or battery aging increases internal resistance, so high-power bursts can drive terminal voltage below cutoff even when substantial charge remains. Monte Carlo simulation yields a full TTE distribution rather than a single countdown, allowing lower-tail risk to be quantified by the 5th percentile. Sensitivity analysis identifies ambient temperature, internal resistance, weak-signal radio penalty, and screen brightness as major drivers of premature shutdown risk. These results motivate practical user guidance and an operating-system-level resistance-aware throttling policy that limits peak power in the power-limited regime. The framework provides a physically grounded, risk-aware approach for explaining and extending usable smartphone battery life under real-world uncertainty.

AI.tldr: A stochastic hybrid automaton combining Thevenin equivalent-circuit, thermal, and user-activity models predicts smartphone time-to-empty distribution, capturing voltage-collapse-driven premature shutdown missed by simpler methods, and motivates resistance-aware throttling policies.
AI.motivation: Smartphone TTE prediction is difficult because shutdown depends not only on remaining charge but also on instantaneous power capability affected by temperature, aging, and load-dependent voltage sag.
AI.method: Develops a stochastic hybrid automaton coupling a first-order Thevenin equivalent-circuit model with a lumped thermal model and a piecewise deterministic Markov process (idle, social/web, video, gaming, weak-signal). Shutdown is a first-passage event when voltage crosses cutoff or power exceeds the feasibility envelope. Monte Carlo simulation generates full TTE distribution.
AI.result: Captures voltage-collapse mechanism; produces TTE distribution enabling lower-tail risk (5th percentile) quantification. Sensitivity analysis identifies ambient temperature, internal resistance, weak-signal radio penalty, and screen brightness as major premature shutdown risk drivers.
AI.conclusion: Framework motivates practical user guidance and an OS-level resistance-aware throttling policy limiting peak power in the power-limited regime, providing a physically grounded, risk-aware approach for extending usable battery life under uncertainty.

title: Towards Trustworthy Audio Deepfake Detection: A Systematic Framework for Diagnosing and Mitigating Gender Bias
summary: Audio deepfake detection systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes security applications, yet their fairness across demographic groups remains critically underexamined. Prior work measures gender disparity but does not investigate where it comes from or how to fix it systematically. We present the first diagnosis-first framework that identifies bias source before applying targeted mitigation, evaluated on two models, AASIST and Wav2Vec2+ResNet18, on ASVSpoof5. Our diagnosis shows that bias does not stem from imbalanced training data but from acoustic representation differences, gender leakage in learned features, and structural evaluation asymmetry. We test mitigation strategies across in-processing, post-processing and combined families, including novel methods introduced in this work. Adjusting the decision threshold separately per gender reduces unfairness by 54% to 75% at no cost to detection accuracy, and our new epoch-level fairness regularisation method outperforms existing per-batch approaches. Adversarial debiasing succeeds only when gender leakage is localised, and fails when it is diffuse, an outcome correctly predicted by our diagnosis before training. No single method fully closes the fairness gap, confirming that bias sources must be identified before fixes are applied and that fairer benchmark design is equally important

AI.tldr: This paper presents a diagnosis-first framework to identify sources of gender bias in audio deepfake detection before applying targeted mitigation. Using AASIST and Wav2Vec2+ResNet18 on ASVSpoof5, they find bias stems from acoustic representation differences, gender leakage, and evaluation asymmetry, not from imbalanced data. Simple threshold adjustment reduces unfairness by 54–75% with no accuracy loss, and their epoch-level fairness regularization outperforms per-batch methods.
AI.motivation: Audio deepfake detection systems are deployed in high-stakes security applications, but their fairness across demographic groups remains critically underexamined. Prior work only measures gender disparity without investigating its origins or providing systematic fixes.
AI.method: A diagnosis-first framework: first identify bias sources (acoustic representation differences, gender leakage in learned features, structural evaluation asymmetry), then apply targeted mitigation strategies across in-processing, post-processing, and combined families, including novel methods. Tested on AASIST and Wav2Vec2+ResNet18 models using ASVSpoof5 dataset.
AI.result: Bias does not originate from imbalanced training data. Per-gender decision threshold adjustment reduces unfairness by 54–75% without accuracy loss. Epoch-level fairness regularization outperforms per-batch approaches. Adversarial debiasing succeeds only when gender leakage is localized. No single method fully closes the fairness gap.
AI.conclusion: Bias sources must be identified before applying fixes; fairer benchmark design is equally important. No single mitigation method is sufficient to fully eliminate fairness gaps.

title: Kinetic-Optimal Scheduling with Moment Correction for Metric-Induced Discrete Flow Matching in Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech
summary: Metric-induced discrete flow matching (MI-DFM) exploits token-latent geometry for discrete generation, but its practical use is limited by two issues: heuristic schedulers requiring hyperparameter search, and finite-step path-tracking error from its first-order continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) solver. We address both issues. First, we derive a kinetic-optimal scheduler for prescribed scalar-parameterized probability paths, and instantiate it for MI-DFM as a training-free numerical schedule that traverses the path at constant Fisher-Rao speed. Second, we introduce a finite-step moment correction that adjusts the jump probability while preserving the CTMC jump destination distribution. We validate the resulting method, GibbsTTS, on codec-based zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS). Under controlled comparisons with a unified architecture and large-scale dataset, GibbsTTS achieves the best objective naturalness and is preferred in subjective evaluations over masked discrete generative baselines. Additionally, in comparison with the evaluated state-of-the-art TTS systems, GibbsTTS shows strong speaker similarity, achieving the highest similarity on three of four test sets and ranking second on the fourth. Project page: https://ydqmkkx.github.io/GibbsTTSProject

AI.tldr: GibbsTTS improves discrete flow matching for text-to-speech by introducing a kinetic-optimal scheduler (constant Fisher-Rao speed) and a finite-step moment correction, achieving state-of-the-art objective naturalness, subjective preference, and strong speaker similarity across multiple test sets.
AI.motivation: Metric-induced discrete flow matching (MI-DFM) has potential for discrete generation but suffers from two practical limitations: (1) heuristic schedulers that require expensive hyperparameter search, and (2) finite-step path-tracking errors caused by its first-order CTMC solver. This work aims to resolve both issues to make MI-DFM practically viable for high-quality generation tasks like zero-shot TTS.
AI.method: The authors propose two key improvements: (1) A kinetic-optimal scheduler derived for prescribed scalar-parameterized probability paths, instantiated for MI-DFM as a training-free numerical schedule that maintains constant Fisher-Rao speed along the path. (2) A finite-step moment correction that adjusts jump probabilities while preserving the CTMC jump destination distribution, reducing discretization error.
AI.result: On codec-based zero-shot TTS with controlled architecture and dataset comparisons, GibbsTTS achieves the best objective naturalness and is preferred in subjective evaluations over masked discrete generative baselines. In comparison with state-of-the-art TTS systems, it achieves the highest speaker similarity on three of four test sets and ranks second on the fourth.
AI.conclusion: The proposed GibbsTTS method effectively addresses the key limitations of MI-DFM through a kinetic-optimal scheduler and moment correction, establishing it as a strong approach for discrete generation, particularly in zero-shot text-to-speech where it achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance.

title: APEX: Audio Prototype EXplanations for Classification Tasks
summary: Explainable AI (XAI) has achieved remarkable success in image classification, yet the audio domain lacks equally mature solutions. Current methods apply vision-based attribution techniques to spectrograms, overlooking fundamental differences between visual and acoustic signals. While prototype reasoning is promising, acoustic similarity remains multidimensional. We introduce APEX (Audio Prototype EXplanations), a post-hoc framework for interpreting pre-trained audio classifiers. Crucially, APEX requires no fine-tuning of the original backbone and strictly preserves output invariance. APEX disentangles explanations into four perspectives: Square-based prototypes to localize transient events, Time-based for temporal patterns, Frequency-based highlighting spectral bands, and Time-Frequency-based integrating both. This yields intuitive, example-based explanations that respect acoustic properties, providing greater semantic clarity than standard gradient-based methods.

AI.tldr: APEX is a post-hoc XAI framework for audio classifiers that provides multi-perspective prototype explanations (square, time, frequency, time-frequency) without modifying the original model, preserving output invariance.
AI.motivation: Audio XAI lags behind vision; existing methods naively apply vision attribution techniques to spectrograms, ignoring the fundamental differences between visual and acoustic signals.
AI.method: APEX disentangles explanations into four prototype-based perspectives: Square-based (transient events), Time-based (temporal patterns), Frequency-based (spectral bands), and Time-Frequency-based (integrated). It is a post-hoc framework requiring no fine-tuning and preserving output invariance.
AI.result: APEX provides intuitive, example-based explanations with greater semantic clarity than standard gradient-based methods, respecting acoustic properties.
AI.conclusion: APEX demonstrates that multi-perspective prototype reasoning tailored to acoustic signal properties yields superior interpretability for pre-trained audio classifiers without sacrificing model fidelity.

title: Evaluating the Expressive Appropriateness of Speech in Rich Contexts
summary: Evaluating expressive speech remains challenging, as existing methods mainly assess emotional intensity and overlook whether a speech sample is expressively appropriate for its contextual setting. This limitation hinders reliable evaluation of speech systems used in narrative-driven and interactive applications, such as audiobooks and conversational agents. We introduce CEAEval, a Context-rich framework for Evaluating Expressive Appropriateness in speech, which assesses whether a speech sample expressively aligns with the underlying communicative intent implied by its discourse-level narrative context. To support this task, we construct CEAEval-D, the first context-rich speech dataset with real human performances in Mandarin conversational speech, providing narrative descriptions together with fifteen dimensions of human annotations covering expressive attributes and expressive appropriateness. We further develop CEAEval-M, a model that integrates knowledge distillation, planner-based multi-model collaboration, adaptive audio attention bias, and reinforcement learning to perform context-rich expressive appropriateness evaluation. Experiments on a human-annotated test set demonstrate that CEAEval-M substantially outperforms existing speech evaluation and analysis systems.

AI.tldr: CEAEval introduces a context-rich framework for evaluating expressive speech appropriateness in narrative-driven and interactive applications, using a new Mandarin conversational dataset (CEAEval-D) with 15 annotation dimensions and a multi-model evaluation system (CEAEval-M) combining knowledge distillation, planner-based collaboration, audio attention bias, and reinforcement learning, outperforming existing methods.
AI.motivation: Existing speech evaluation methods focus on emotional intensity but fail to assess whether a speech sample is expressively appropriate for its contextual setting, which is critical for narrative-driven and interactive applications like audiobooks and conversational agents.
AI.method: The authors created CEAEval-D, the first context-rich speech dataset with real Mandarin conversational performances, narrative descriptions, and 15 human-annotated dimensions. They then developed CEAEval-M, a model integrating knowledge distillation, planner-based multi-model collaboration, adaptive audio attention bias, and reinforcement learning for context-rich expressive appropriateness evaluation.
AI.result: CEAEval-M substantially outperforms existing speech evaluation and analysis systems on a human-annotated test set.
AI.conclusion: CEAEval addresses the overlooked aspect of contextual expressive appropriateness in speech evaluation, providing both a dataset and a model that significantly advance the assessment of expressive speech in context-rich settings.

title: Safe Exploration for Nonlinear Processes Using Online Gaussian Process Learning
summary: This paper proposes a safe data-driven control framework for nonlinear systems with partially known dynamics. The method ensures stability and constraint satisfaction during online learning, assuming only a stabilizable linear approximation of the process is available. Unmodeled nonlinear dynamics are captured by a Gaussian process residual learned in real time. Safety is enforced through a probabilistic control-invariant set derived from Lyapunov theory, guaranteeing high-probability stability. A convex quadratic program computes control inputs that maximize information gain while respecting probabilistic safety constraints. The framework provides finite-sample safety guarantees and allows adaptive expansion of the invariant set as uncertainty decreases. Numerical results validate the approach, demonstrating safe and informative exploration under model uncertainty: the safe set expands by about 30% while the Gaussian process root-mean-square error drops from 1.11 to 0.03.

AI.tldr: A safe data-driven control framework for nonlinear systems using Gaussian process residuals and Lyapunov-based probabilistic safety guarantees, enabling safe exploration and adaptive expansion of invariant sets.
AI.motivation: To enable safe online learning and control for nonlinear systems with partially known dynamics, where only a stabilizable linear approximation is available and unmodeled dynamics must be captured in real time without violating safety constraints.
AI.method: Combines a Gaussian process residual to model unmodeled nonlinear dynamics online, uses Lyapunov theory to derive a probabilistic control-invariant set for safety, and solves a convex quadratic program to maximize information gain under probabilistic safety constraints.
AI.result: The safe set expands by about 30% and the Gaussian process root-mean-square error drops from 1.11 to 0.03 during online learning.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework achieves safe and informative exploration under model uncertainty with finite-sample safety guarantees and adaptive expansion of the invariant set as uncertainty decreases.

title: Polyphonia: Zero-Shot Timbre Transfer in Polyphonic Music with Acoustic-Informed Attention Calibration
summary: The advancement of diffusion-based text-to-music generation has opened new avenues for zero-shot music editing. However, existing methods fail to achieve stem-specific timbre transfer, which requires altering specific stems while strictly preserving the background accompaniment. This limitation severely hinders practical application, since real-world production necessitates precise manipulation of components within dense mixtures. Our key finding is that, while vanilla cross-attention captures semantic features of stems, it lacks the spectral resolution to strictly localize targets in dense mixtures, leading to boundary leakage. To resolve this dilemma, we propose Polyphonia, a zero-shot editing framework with Acoustic-Informed Attention Calibration. Rather than relying solely on diffuse semantic attention, Polyphonia leverages a probabilistic acoustic prior to establish coarse boundaries, enabling non-target stems preserved precise semantic synthesis. For evaluation, we propose PolyEvalPrompts, a standardized prompt set with 1,170 timbre transfer tasks in polyphonic music. Specifically, Polyphonia achieves an increase of 15.5% in target alignment compared to baselines, while maintaining competitive music fidelity and non-target integrity.

AI.tldr: Polyphonia is a zero-shot music editing framework that uses Acoustic-Informed Attention Calibration to achieve stem-specific timbre transfer in polyphonic music, improving target alignment by 15.5% while preserving background accompaniment.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based text-to-music generation methods cannot achieve stem-specific timbre transfer—altering specific stems while strictly preserving background accompaniment—due to boundary leakage in vanilla cross-attention, which lacks spectral resolution for dense mixtures.
AI.method: Polyphonia introduces Acoustic-Informed Attention Calibration, leveraging a probabilistic acoustic prior to establish coarse boundaries for target stems, enabling precise semantic synthesis while preserving non-target stems.
AI.result: Polyphonia achieves a 15.5% increase in target alignment over baselines while maintaining competitive music fidelity and non-target integrity on PolyEvalPrompts, a newly proposed standardized prompt set of 1,170 timbre transfer tasks.
AI.conclusion: Acoustic-informed attention calibration effectively resolves the boundary leakage problem in dense polyphonic mixtures, enabling practical stem-specific timbre transfer for real-world music production.

title: RADAR Challenge 2026: Robust Audio Deepfake Recognition under Media Transformations
summary: RADAR Challenge 2026 is an APSIPA Grand Challenge on Robust Audio Deepfake Recognition under Media Transformations, designed to simulate realistic media conditions in real-world audio distribution pipelines, including compression, resampling, noise, and reverberation. It consists of two phases: an English development phase with labeled data for analysis and paper writing, and a multilingual evaluation phase containing more than 100,000 utterances in English, Singapore English, Mandarin Chinese, Taiwanese Mandarin, Japanese, and Vietnamese. Systems are evaluated using equal error rate (EER) for binary real/fake classification. This paper describes the challenge task, the construction of the data set, the evaluation protocol, and the overall results. During the challenge, 33 teams submitted to the development phase and 22 teams submitted to the final evaluation phase. The reported results highlight the remaining challenges of robust audio deepfake detection under multilingual and media-transformed conditions.

AI.tldr: RADAR Challenge 2026 is a grand challenge on robust audio deepfake recognition under media transformations (compression, resampling, noise, reverberation), featuring multilingual evaluation across 6 languages with 100k+ utterances. 33 teams participated in development and 22 in final evaluation, highlighting ongoing difficulties in robust audio deepfake detection.
AI.motivation: To address the gap between controlled laboratory conditions and real-world audio distribution pipelines by simulating realistic media transformations (compression, resampling, noise, reverberation) that audio deepfake detection systems must withstand.
AI.method: A two-phase challenge: (1) English development phase with labeled data for analysis and paper writing, (2) multilingual evaluation phase with >100,000 utterances across English, Singapore English, Mandarin Chinese, Taiwanese Mandarin, Japanese, and Vietnamese. Systems evaluated using equal error rate (EER) for binary real/fake classification.
AI.result: 33 teams submitted to the development phase and 22 teams submitted to the final evaluation phase. Results revealed remaining challenges in robust audio deepfake detection under multilingual and media-transformed conditions.
AI.conclusion: Robust audio deepfake detection remains challenging under multilingual and media-transformed conditions, indicating a need for further research on generalization across languages and resilience to real-world media distortions.

title: Action Recommendations for Sequentially Rational Strategic Agents
summary: We consider a finite-horizon discrete-time dynamic system that is jointly controlled by two strategic agents. There is a system designer that has its own reward function but does not have direct control over the agents' actions. We consider an information structure where the current state and all past history are equally accessible by the designer and the agents. The designer sends action recommendations to the agents at each time step. Each agent can use the received recommendation and the available information to choose its action. We are interested in the setting where the designer would like to send recommendations in a way that incentivizes the agents to adopt obedient strategies, i.e., to take the action recommended by the designer. Our goal is to find an optimal action recommendation strategy for the designer that maximizes the designer's objective while ensuring that obedient strategies are \emph{sequentially rational} for the agents. We provide an algorithm for the designer's problem that involves solving a family of linear programs in a backward inductive manner.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a finite-horizon discrete-time dynamic system controlled by two strategic agents and a system designer who sends action recommendations. The goal is to find an optimal recommendation strategy that maximizes the designer's reward while ensuring sequential rationality (obedience) for the agents, solved via backward-inductive linear programming.
AI.motivation: The designer has its own reward function but cannot directly control the agents' actions. The key challenge is to design a recommendation strategy that incentivizes agents to follow recommendations sequentially over time, ensuring obedience is in each agent's rational self-interest at every stage.
AI.method: The problem is formulated as a finite-horizon dynamic system with symmetric information. The designer's optimal recommendation strategy is solved by a backward inductive algorithm that solves a family of linear programs at each time step, enforcing sequential rationality constraints for both agents.
AI.result: An algorithm is provided that computes the optimal action recommendation strategy for the designer by solving linear programs in a backward inductive manner, ensuring the agents' obedient strategies are sequentially rational.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a computational approach (via linear programming and backward induction) for a designer to optimally influence strategic agents' behavior through recommendations while maintaining incentive compatibility over time.

title: A Cold Diffusion Approach for Percussive Dereverberation
comment: Accepted for the 2026 IEEE World Congress on Computational Intelligence, IJCNN Track, 21-26 June 2026, Maastricht, the Netherlands
summary: Most recent advances in audio dereverberation focus almost exclusively on speech, leaving percussive and drum signals largely unexplored despite their importance in music production. Percussive dereverberation poses distinct challenges due to sharp transients and dense temporal structure. In this work, we propose a cold diffusion framework for dereverberating stereo drum stems (downmixes), modeling reverberation as a deterministic degradation process that progressively transforms anechoic signals into reverberant ones. We investigate two reverse-process parameterizations, Direct (next-state) and a Delta-normalized residual (velocity-style) prediction, and implement the framework using both a UNet and a diffusion Transformer backbone. The models are trained and evaluated on curated datasets comprising both acoustic and electronic drum recordings, with reverberation generated using a combination of synthetic and real room impulse responses. Extensive experiments on in-domain and fully out-of-domain test sets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms strong score-based and conditional diffusion baselines, evaluated using signal-based and perceptual metrics tailored to percussive audio.

AI.tldr: Proposes a cold diffusion framework for dereverberating stereo drum stems, outperforming score-based and conditional diffusion baselines on both in-domain and out-of-domain test sets.
AI.motivation: Audio dereverberation has focused almost exclusively on speech; percussive and drum signals remain largely unexplored despite their importance in music production. Percussive dereverberation poses distinct challenges due to sharp transients and dense temporal structure.
AI.method: A cold diffusion framework modeling reverberation as a deterministic degradation process that progressively transforms anechoic signals into reverberant ones. Two reverse-process parameterizations (Direct next-state and Delta-normalized residual/velocity-style prediction) are investigated, implemented with both a UNet and a diffusion Transformer backbone.
AI.result: Consistently outperforms strong score-based and conditional diffusion baselines on in-domain and fully out-of-domain test sets, evaluated using signal-based and perceptual metrics tailored to percussive audio.
AI.conclusion: The proposed cold diffusion framework is effective for drum stem dereverberation, handling sharp transients and dense temporal structure better than existing diffusion-based approaches.

title: Single-Microphone Audio Point Source Discriminative Localization From Reverberation Late Tail Estimation
summary: Location information can be a valuable signal for audio segmentation tasks, especially as a complement to methods focusing on the content or qualities of the sources. Though audio source localization is typically performed using the observations of the signal captured by multiple microphones in space, information about a source's location is captured by a single microphone through its arrival time and spectral amplitude--given the source's emitted signal is known. Since reverberation originates from the audio sources in a room, it accordingly contains some information about the emitted audio signals. The late-tail part of reverberation is relatively invariant to the local source and microphone geometry, depending primarily on only the room itself, and thus can provide the necessary reference information about audio signals that depends minimally on their location. In this work, we leverage the robust late-tail estimation of Weighted Prediction Error (WPE) dereverberation within a probabilistic framework to estimate the likelihood of two audio signals collected in the same room as having originated from the same location. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on the speaker diarization task in both simulated and real environments.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using late-tail reverberation estimates from WPE dereverberation to determine if two audio signals originate from the same location, and demonstrates its effectiveness for speaker diarization in simulated and real environments.
AI.motivation: Location information is valuable for audio segmentation tasks but is typically obtained via multiple microphones. The authors aim to leverage single-microphone location cues through reverberation properties, specifically the invariant late-tail reverberation, to complement content-based methods.
AI.method: The approach uses robust late-tail estimation from Weighted Prediction Error (WPE) dereverberation within a probabilistic framework to estimate the likelihood that two audio signals recorded in the same room originated from the same spatial location.
AI.result: The method is demonstrated to be effective for speaker diarization in both simulated and real acoustic environments.
AI.conclusion: Late-tail reverberation, being invariant to local source/microphone geometry, provides a useful reference signal for location-based audio segmentation. The WPE-based probabilistic approach successfully leverages this invariance for single-microphone location inference.

title: Dynamic Scheduling of a Parallel-Server Queueing System: A Computational Method for High-Dimensional Problems
summary: A key operational challenge for call centers is to decide, in real time, which waiting customer should be served by which available agent. This is known as skill-based routing, and the decision becomes especially difficult in large systems with many customer classes, where standard dynamic programming methods can be computationally intractable. Focusing on the Halfin-Whitt heavy-traffic regime and an infinite-horizon discounted cost criterion, we develop a computational method that scales to high-dimensional settings with many customer classes. Our approach begins by deriving an approximating diffusion control problem in the heavy traffic limiting regime. Building on earlier work by Han et al. (2018), we develop a simulation-based method to solve this problem, relying heavily on deep neural network techniques. Using this framework, we construct a policy for the original (prelimit) call center scheduling problem. To evaluate performance, we adopt a data-driven approach. Using call center data from a large U.S. bank, we calibrate the model and construct realistic test instances. We then compare the resulting policy with benchmark policies drawn from the literature. Across all test problems considered so far, our policy performs at least as well as or better than the best benchmark identified. Moreover, the method remains computationally feasible in dimensions up to 100, corresponding to call centers with 100 or more distinct customer classes.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a scalable, deep neural network-based method for skill-based routing in large call centers, using heavy-traffic diffusion approximations and data-driven calibration from a U.S. bank, achieving strong performance in settings with up to 100 customer classes.
AI.motivation: Real-time skill-based routing in large call centers with many customer classes is computationally intractable for standard dynamic programming methods, creating a need for scalable solutions.
AI.method: The authors derive an approximating diffusion control problem in the Halfin-Whitt heavy-traffic regime, then develop a simulation-based method using deep neural networks to solve it, and construct a policy for the original call center scheduling problem.
AI.result: The proposed policy performs at least as well as or better than the best benchmark across all test problems, and remains computationally feasible in dimensions up to 100 customer classes, validated using real call center data from a large U.S. bank.
AI.conclusion: Deep neural network-based diffusion control provides an effective and scalable approach to skill-based routing in high-dimensional call centers, with strong empirical performance and practical feasibility.

title: Drum Synthesis from Expressive Drum Grids via Neural Audio Codecs
summary: Generating realistic drum audio directly from symbolic representations is a challenging task at the intersection of music perception and machine learning. We propose a system that transforms an expressive drum grid, a time-aligned MIDI representation with microtiming and velocity information, into drum audio by predicting discrete codes of a neural audio codec. Our approach uses a Transformer-based model to map the drum grid input to a sequence of codec tokens, which are then converted to waveform audio via a pre-trained codec decoder. We experiment with multiple state-of-the-art neural codecs, namely EnCodec, DAC, and X-Codec, to assess how the choice of audio representation impacts the quality of the generated drums. The system is trained and evaluated on the Expanded Groove MIDI Dataset, E-GMD, a large collection of human drum performances with paired MIDI and audio. We evaluate the fidelity and musical alignment of the generated audio using objective metrics. Overall, our results establish codec-token prediction as an effective route for drum grid-to-audio generation and provide practical insights into selecting audio tokenizers for percussive synthesis.

AI.tldr: A Transformer-based system generates drum audio from expressive MIDI drum grids by predicting discrete codes from neural audio codecs (EnCodec, DAC, X-Codec), trained and evaluated on the E-GMD dataset.
AI.motivation: Generating realistic drum audio from symbolic representations (e.g., MIDI) is challenging due to the gap between discrete note-level information and continuous audio signals, requiring methods that preserve musical expressiveness like microtiming and velocity.
AI.method: A Transformer model takes an expressive drum grid (MIDI with microtiming and velocity) as input and predicts discrete codec tokens from pre-trained neural audio codecs (EnCodec, DAC, X-Codec). The predicted tokens are decoded into waveform audio via the codec decoder.
AI.result: Codec-token prediction proves effective for drum grid-to-audio generation; the study provides objective fidelity and musical alignment metrics, and compares three different neural codecs for percussive synthesis.
AI.conclusion: Codec-token prediction is a viable approach for symbolic-to-audio drum generation, with practical insights on selecting audio tokenizers for percussive sounds.

title: PoDAR: Power-Disentangled Audio Representation for Generative Modeling
summary: The performance of audio latent diffusion models is primarily governed by generator expressivity and the modelability of the underlying latent space. While recent research has focused primarily on the former, as well as improving the reconstruction fidelity of audio codecs, we demonstrate that latent modelability can be significantly improved through explicit factor disentanglement. We present PoDAR (Power-Disentangled Audio Representation), a framework that utilizes a randomized power augmentation and latent consistency objective to decouple signal power from invariant semantic content. This factorization makes the latent space easier to model, which both accelerates the convergence of downstream generative models and improves final overall performance. When applied to a Stable Audio 1.0 VAE with an F5-TTS generator, PoDAR achieves about a $2\times$ acceleration in convergence to match baseline performance, while increasing final speaker similarity by 0.055 and UTMOS by 0.22 on the LibriSpeech-PC dataset. Furthermore, isolating power into dedicated channels enables the application of CFG exclusively to power-invariant content, effectively extending the stable guidance regime to higher scales.

AI.tldr: PoDAR improves latent diffusion model performance by disentangling signal power from semantic content, accelerating convergence ~2x and improving speaker similarity by 0.055 and UTMOS by 0.22 on LibriSpeech-PC.
AI.motivation: Current audio latent diffusion models focus on generator expressivity and codec reconstruction fidelity, but neglect the modelability of the latent space itself. The authors aim to show that explicit factor disentanglement can significantly improve latent modelability.
AI.method: PoDAR uses randomized power augmentation and a latent consistency objective to decouple signal power from invariant semantic content in the latent space, applied to a Stable Audio 1.0 VAE with an F5-TTS generator.
AI.result: ~2x convergence acceleration matching baseline performance; +0.055 speaker similarity; +0.22 UTMOS on LibriSpeech-PC. Isolating power also enables CFG to be applied exclusively to power-invariant content, extending stable guidance to higher scales.
AI.conclusion: Explicit power disentanglement improves latent modelability, accelerates training, and enhances downstream generative performance, while also enabling more stable classifier-free guidance at higher scales.

title: Geometric Pareto Control: Riemannian Gradient Flow of Energy Function via Lie Group Homotopy
summary: We propose Geometric Pareto Control (GPC), a framework overcoming barriers of reinforcement learning in cyber-physical systems where governing physics is known. Reinforcement learning confronts barriers in safety-critical applications: sample complexity grows with action-space dimension, retraining is required when objectives or conditions shift, goals such as safety recovery and economic dispatch demand brittle switching logic, and unsafe exploration persists under constrained RL formulations. GPC resolves these barriers through a two-stage geometric approach. Offline, the supported family of Pareto-optimal solutions (i.e., solutions recoverable by weighted scalarization) is embedded as a submanifold within a Lie group. Exponential map closure preserves membership in the ambient Lie group; drift and reset assumptions keep online latent states within a bounded neighbourhood of the Pareto submanifold, and a training-time feasibility margin guarantees decoded actions remain feasible without post-hoc projection, constructing a "map" of the solution landscape. Online, a closed-form proximal navigator traverses this submanifold via a unified Riemannian gradient flow driven by a singular perturbation potential field, inducing dual-timescale dynamics that prioritize constraint restoration over performance optimization. The homeomorphic structure of the submanifold guarantees that varying system parameters and objective weights produce continuous control actions, enabling deployment under unseen conditions without retraining. Validated on a nonconvex control task and real-time multi-objective optimal power flow, GPC achieves 100% feasibility, 0.30% oracle suboptimality, and 12.3 ms decisions while shifting from constraint recovery to economic dispatch. Under branch-admittance uncertainty, it remains 100% feasible without retraining, whereas model-free baselines produce no feasible dispatches.

AI.tldr: GPC is a two-stage geometric framework that embeds Pareto-optimal solutions as a Lie-group submanifold offline and uses a closed-form Riemannian gradient flow navigator online to achieve safe, zero-retraining, real-time control in cyber-physical systems with known physics.
AI.motivation: Reinforcement learning in safety-critical cyber-physical systems suffers from high sample complexity, need for retraining under shifting objectives/conditions, brittle switching logic for safety recovery vs. economic dispatch, and unsafe exploration under constrained RL.
AI.method: Offline: embed the family of Pareto-optimal solutions as a submanifold within a Lie group using exponential map closure. Online: traverse the submanifold via a closed-form proximal navigator using a Riemannian gradient flow driven by a singular perturbation potential field, inducing dual-timescale dynamics prioritizing constraint restoration over performance.
AI.result: On nonconvex control and real-time multi-objective optimal power flow: 100% feasibility, 0.30% oracle suboptimality, 12.3 ms decisions, seamless shift from constraint recovery to economic dispatch. Under branch-admittance uncertainty: 100% feasibility without retraining; model-free baselines produce no feasible dispatches.
AI.conclusion: GPC effectively eliminates key RL barriers (retraining, unsafe exploration, brittle switching) in known-physics CPS by leveraging geometric structure, achieving safe, continuous, and real-time multi-objective control under uncertainty.

title: Multi-layer attentive probing improves transfer of audio representations for bioacoustics
summary: Probing heads map the representations learned from audio by a machine learning model to downstream task labels and are a key component in evaluating representation learning. Most bioacoustic benchmarks use a fixed, low-capacity probe, such as a linear layer on the final encoder layer. While this standardization enables model comparisons, it may bias results by overlooking the interaction between encoder features and probe design. In this work, we systematically study different probing strategies across two bioacoustic benchmarks, BEANs and BirdSet. We evaluate last- and multi-layer probing, across linear and attention probes. We show that larger probe heads that leverage time information have superior performance. Our results suggest that current benchmarks may misrepresent encoder quality when relying on a last-layer probing setup. Multi-layer probing improves downstream task performance across all tested models, while attention probing has superior performance to linear probing for transformer models.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically studies probing strategies in bioacoustic benchmarks, showing that multi-layer and attention probes outperform standard last-layer linear probes, suggesting current benchmarks may misrepresent encoder quality.
AI.motivation: Most bioacoustic benchmarks use a fixed, low-capacity linear probe on the final encoder layer, which may bias results by overlooking the interaction between encoder features and probe design, potentially misrepresenting true encoder quality.
AI.method: Systematic comparison of probing strategies (last-layer vs. multi-layer, linear vs. attention probes) across two bioacoustic benchmarks (BEANs and BirdSet) on various models.
AI.result: Larger probe heads leveraging time information achieve superior performance. Multi-layer probing improves performance across all models. Attention probing outperforms linear probing for transformer models.
AI.conclusion: Current benchmarks may misrepresent encoder quality when relying solely on last-layer linear probing. Multi-layer and attention-based probing strategies are recommended for fairer evaluation.

title: SF-Flow: Sound field magnitude estimation via flow matching guided by sparse measurements
summary: Reconstructing a 3D sound field from sparse microphone measurements is a fundamental yet ill-posed problem, which we address through Acoustic Transfer Function (ATF) magnitude estimation. ATF magnitude encapsulates key perceptual and acoustic properties of a physical space with applications in room characterization and correction. Although recent generative paradigms such as Flow Matching (FM) have achieved state-of-the-art performance in speech and music generation, their potential in spatial audio remains underexplored. We propose a novel framework for 3D ATF magnitude reconstruction as a guided generation task, with a 3D U-Net conditioned by a permutation-invariant set encoder. This architecture enables reconstruction from an arbitrary number of sparse inputs while leveraging the stable and efficient training properties of FM. Experimental results demonstrate that SF-Flow achieves accurate reconstruction up to \SI{1}{kHz}, trains substantially faster than the autoencoder baseline, and improves significantly with dataset size.

AI.tldr: Proposes SF-Flow, a Flow Matching framework for 3D Acoustic Transfer Function magnitude reconstruction from sparse microphone measurements using a 3D U-Net conditioned on a permutation-invariant set encoder, achieving accurate reconstruction up to 1 kHz with faster training than autoencoder baselines.
AI.motivation: Reconstructing 3D sound fields from sparse microphone measurements is ill-posed; existing generative approaches (e.g., Flow Matching) have shown success in speech/music but remain unexplored for spatial audio reconstruction.
AI.method: Formulates ATF magnitude reconstruction as a guided generation task using Flow Matching with a 3D U-Net backbone conditioned by a permutation-invariant set encoder, enabling arbitrary sparse input configurations.
AI.result: Accurate reconstruction up to 1 kHz; substantially faster training than autoencoder baseline; performance scales significantly with dataset size.
AI.conclusion: Flow Matching is an effective and efficient paradigm for 3D sound field reconstruction from sparse measurements, offering advantages in training speed and scalability.

title: Harnessing Floating Car Data, Traffic Camera Observations, and Network Flow Analysis for Traffic Volume Estimation
comment: This manuscript is a preprint version of a work submitted to Discover Civil Engineering
summary: Cities increasingly rely on vehicle trajectory data to monitor traffic conditions; however, such data offer only a partial and spatially heterogeneous view of network dynamics and exhibit systematic biases across corridors and time periods. In contrast, surveillance cameras can provide high-fidelity traffic information, but only at a limited set of locations, typically sparsely distributed across the road network. We present a hybrid modeling and calibration framework that fuses these complementary data sources to produce physically consistent, network-wide estimates and short-horizon forecasts of traffic volumes. The framework leverages kinematic features derived from the Cell Transmission Model (CTM) formulation within a graph neural network (GNN). By enforcing traffic-flow conservation, capacity limits, and spillback dynamics, the CTM provides a physically grounded representation of traffic flow, while the GNN learns the spatiotemporal evolution of traffic states over the entire road network. To calibrate the model predictions on traffic camera observations, we use a progressive data-assimilation scheme based on an Ensemble Square-Root Kalman filter (EnSRF). A topology-informed flow-weighted transition matrix is further employed to propagate camera-driven corrections to unobserved road segments, enabling real-time, network-wide traffic state and volume estimation. The approach is demonstrated using probe-vehicle trajectory data and municipal traffic cameras in Manhattan, New York City, where it achieves improved accuracy relative to trajectory-based estimates while maintaining physically plausible and network-consistent traffic flows. The proposed framework accommodates varying sensor availability and produces calibrated traffic volumes with uncertainty estimates, supporting operational monitoring and evaluation of transportation policies in data-constrained urban environments.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a hybrid framework that fuses vehicle trajectory data and surveillance camera data using a CTM-informed GNN with EnSRF-based data assimilation to produce physically consistent, network-wide traffic volume estimates and forecasts, demonstrated on Manhattan, NYC data.
AI.motivation: Vehicle trajectory data provide only partial, spatially heterogeneous, and biased views of network traffic, while surveillance cameras offer high-fidelity information only at sparse locations. The authors aim to fuse these complementary data sources to overcome their individual limitations.
AI.method: A hybrid modeling and calibration framework combining: (1) CTM kinematic features embedded within a GNN for physically grounded traffic flow representation; (2) EnSRF-based progressive data assimilation for calibrating predictions on camera observations; (3) a topology-informed flow-weighted transition matrix to propagate corrections to unobserved segments.
AI.result: The approach achieves improved accuracy over trajectory-based estimates in Manhattan, NYC, while maintaining physically plausible and network-consistent traffic flows with uncertainty estimates.
AI.conclusion: The framework accommodates varying sensor availability, produces calibrated volumes with uncertainty estimates, and supports operational monitoring and policy evaluation in data-constrained urban environments.

title: ShipEcho -- An Interactive Tool for Global Mapping of Underwater Radiated Noise from Vessels
summary: Underwater radiated noise from vessels (V-URN) is a recognized environmental stressor that negatively impacts marine ecosystems. Significant resources are invested in the development of V-URN monitoring indicators, regulatory frameworks, and management-oriented assessments. One approach with high potential for impact is V-URN mapping, which can provide actionable spatiotemporal information for environmental assessment and mitigation planning. Producing management-scale maps remains challenging as passive acoustic measurements are spatially sparse and many operational systems depend on specialist workflows and costly access to wide-area vessel activity data. To address these constraints, we introduce ShipEcho, a freely accessible web-based Geographic Information System (GIS) that provides near-real-time V-URN mapping using vessel data acquired through a community-based AIS exchange. Using established vessel SL models and propagation modeling informed by bathymetric data, ShipEcho produces near-real-time and cumulative noise maps across regions worldwide. These include sound pressure levels and sound exposure levels using standard indicators, including the 63~Hz and 125~Hz one-third octave bands and a 20--2000~Hz broadband level. We describe the system architecture, data pipeline, modeling workflow, and key assumptions, and evaluate map accuracy through comparison with acoustic recordings. We then demonstrate how ShipEcho can support management-level assessment, decision-making, and policy initiatives through practical use cases.

AI.tldr: ShipEcho is a free web-based GIS that provides near-real-time underwater radiated noise mapping from vessels using community-based AIS data, standard sound propagation models, and bathymetric information to support environmental management and policy.
AI.motivation: V-URN is a recognized environmental stressor, but producing management-scale noise maps remains challenging due to spatially sparse acoustic measurements, reliance on specialist workflows, and costly access to vessel activity data.
AI.method: ShipEcho integrates community-based AIS vessel data with established source level models and propagation modeling informed by bathymetry, delivered via a freely accessible web GIS platform. It generates near-real-time and cumulative noise maps using standard indicators (63 Hz, 125 Hz one-third octave bands, 20–2000 Hz broadband).
AI.result: The system produces spatiotemporal V-URN maps globally, with accuracy evaluated through comparison with acoustic recordings. Practical use cases demonstrate support for management-level assessment, decision-making, and policy initiatives.
AI.conclusion: ShipEcho addresses key constraints in V-URN mapping by providing a freely accessible, scalable solution that lowers barriers to entry and delivers actionable noise information for environmental management and regulatory frameworks.

title: Optimal Loss Reduction in Distribution Networks Using Conservation Voltage Reduction and Network Topology Reconfiguration
summary: Conservation voltage reduction (CVR) and network topology reconfiguration (NTR) are widely employed to improve distribution system performance; however, existing approaches largely treat them independently, overlooking their coupled impact on load demand, voltage profiles, and power flow distribution, thereby limiting their overall effectiveness. This paper proposes a coordinated optimization framework for day-ahead operational planning of distribution networks, integrating CVR and NTR to enhance overall network efficiency and reduce active power losses in radial distribution networks. The problem is formulated as a mixed-integer conic programming model incorporating AC power flow constraints, voltage-dependent load representation, and radiality constraints. CVR is implemented to achieve load reduction through coordinated voltage control, while NTR redistributes line loading via optimal switching of controllable branches. The proposed framework is validated on the IEEE 33 and 123-bus distribution systems under varying load conditions. Results demonstrate that the coordinated approach consistently outperforms independent strategies, achieving up to 20.6% reduction in active power losses while maintaining voltage compliance and improving branch loading uniformity. These findings confirm that coordinated optimization provides an effective and scalable solution for enhancing efficiency in modern distribution networks.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a coordinated day-ahead optimization framework integrating Conservation Voltage Reduction (CVR) and Network Topology Reconfiguration (NTR) for distribution networks, formulated as a mixed-integer conic programming model, achieving up to 20.6% reduction in active power losses validated on IEEE 33 and 123-bus systems.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches treat CVR and NTR independently, overlooking their coupled impact on load demand, voltage profiles, and power flow distribution, which limits overall effectiveness in improving distribution system performance.
AI.method: The problem is formulated as a mixed-integer conic programming model incorporating AC power flow constraints, voltage-dependent load representation, and radiality constraints, integrating CVR via coordinated voltage control and NTR via optimal switching of controllable branches for day-ahead operational planning.
AI.result: Validated on IEEE 33 and 123-bus systems under varying load conditions; coordinated approach achieves up to 20.6% reduction in active power losses while maintaining voltage compliance and improving branch loading uniformity compared to independent strategies.
AI.conclusion: Coordinated optimization of CVR and NTR provides an effective and scalable solution for enhancing efficiency in modern distribution networks.

title: Bangla-WhisperDiar: Fine-Tuning Whisper and PyAnnote for Bangla Long-Form Speech Recognition and Speaker Diarization
summary: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and speaker diarization in Bangla remain challenging due to long form recordings, diverse acoustic conditions, and significant speaker variability. This work addresses these two core tasks in Bangla spoken language understanding by developing robust systems for long form ASR and speaker diarization. For ASR (Problem 1), we fine tune the tugstugi bengaliai regional asr whisper medium model on a custom-curated dataset of approximately 15,000 chunked and aligned Bangla audio segments, employing full weight training with extensive data augmentation including noise injection, reverb simulation, echo, clipping distortion, and pitch/time perturbation. For speaker diarization (Problem 2), we fine-tune the pyannote/segmentation-3.0 model using PyTorch Lightning on the competition annotated diarization dataset, swapping the fine-tuned segmentation backbone into the pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1 pipeline while retaining the pretrained speaker embedding and clustering components. Our ASR system achieves a Word Error Rate (WER) of 0.2441, while our diarization system achieves a Diarization Error Rate (DER) of 0.2392, both evaluated on the test set, demonstrating notable improvements over the respective pretrained baselines. We describe our complete pipeline, including data preprocessing, text normalization, audio augmentation, training strategies, inference optimization, and post-processing for both tasks.

AI.tldr: This paper develops robust Bangla ASR and speaker diarization systems by fine-tuning whisper-medium and pyannote/segmentation-3.0 models on custom datasets, achieving WER of 0.2441 and DER of 0.2392 respectively.
AI.motivation: Bangla ASR and speaker diarization remain challenging due to long-form recordings, diverse acoustic conditions, and significant speaker variability, motivating the need for robust systems.
AI.method: For ASR, fine-tune tugstugi/bengaliai-regional-asr-whisper-medium on ~15K Bangla audio segments with full weight training and data augmentation (noise, reverb, echo, clipping, pitch/time perturbation). For diarization, fine-tune pyannote/segmentation-3.0 with PyTorch Lightning on competition data, then swap the segmentation backbone into the speaker-diarization-community-1 pipeline.
AI.result: ASR achieves WER of 0.2441; diarization achieves DER of 0.2392 on the test set, both outperforming pretrained baselines.
AI.conclusion: The proposed pipelines with fine-tuning and augmentation yield notable improvements for Bangla ASR and speaker diarization over baseline models.

title: Scalable Design of Attack-Resilient Controllers for Positive Systems
comment: 3 figures, submitted to L-CSS and CDC 2026
summary: This paper proposes a framework for secure and resilient controller design for positive systems against cyber-attacks. In particular, we consider a network-controlled system where an adversary injects false data into the actuator channels to increase the control cost (performance measure) while penalizing the attack effort and subject to state-dependent constraints. Using a minimax formulation, we analyze the worst-case performance loss caused by such adversaries, which is given by the solution of a difference equation, and an algebraic equation when the time horizon is infinite. We show that the optimal attack policy, among possible nonlinear policies, is linear. Despite the lack of explicit stealthiness constraints, we also show that when the measured output has an unstable zero which is not an unstable zero of the performance measure, the attacks can induce unbounded performance degradation. The proposed framework is also extended to systems with model uncertainty. Numerical examples illustrate the results and demonstrate how tools from positive systems and linear regulator theory can be used to mitigate cyber-attacks with low computational effort.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a minimax-based framework for designing secure and resilient controllers for positive systems facing false data injection attacks on actuator channels, showing optimal attacks are linear and can cause unbounded performance degradation under certain conditions, with extensions to model uncertainty.
AI.motivation: To address the vulnerability of networked positive systems to cyber-attacks where adversaries inject false data into actuator channels to degrade control performance, and to develop a framework that quantifies worst-case performance loss and enables resilient controller design.
AI.method: Uses a minimax formulation to analyze worst-case performance loss under state-dependent constraints; solves difference equations (finite horizon) and algebraic equations (infinite horizon); extends analysis to systems with model uncertainty; leverages tools from positive systems and linear regulator theory.
AI.result: The optimal attack policy among nonlinear policies is linear. When the measured output has an unstable zero that is not an unstable zero of the performance measure, attacks can cause unbounded performance degradation. The framework successfully extends to uncertain systems.
AI.conclusion: The proposed minimax framework effectively models and mitigates cyber-attacks on positive systems, with the key insight that optimal attacks are linear and certain structural properties (unstable zeros) can lead to catastrophic degradation, while positive systems theory enables computationally efficient mitigation.

title: Delay-Robust Secondary Frequency Control via Passive Interconnection and Randomized Block Updates
summary: This paper studies secondary frequency control in transmission networks subject to communication delays at the cyber-physical interface and limited per-update computation at the control center. The regulation objective is formulated as a constrained economic dispatch problem incorporating generation capacity constraints, nodal power balance, transmission-flow limits, and scheduled tie-line power exchanges. Based on this formulation, we develop a passivity-based control framework in which an augmented projected primal-dual controller restores nominal frequency and drives the closed-loop system to the solution set of the constrained economic dispatch problem. Two-way communication delays between the physical network and the control center are modeled as scattering-based passive channels for the measurement uplink and the control-command downlink. This construction preserves the target equilibrium and enables a delay-robust passivity analysis of the delayed closed loop. To reduce the computational burden at the control center, we develop a randomized block-coordinate implementation of the augmented projected primal-dual controller. The resulting sampled-data closed loop preserves the target solution set and achieves local mean-square geometric convergence under suitable step-size and regularity conditions. Finally, a multivariable wave-domain interface filter is introduced to inject additional dissipation and improve the damping of the delayed interface without altering the steady-state interconnection. Simulations on the IEEE 14-bus system indicate that the proposed digital implementation accurately reproduces the delayed closed-loop behavior while reducing the per-update computational cost.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a passivity-based control framework for secondary frequency control in transmission networks that handles communication delays via scattering-based passive channels and reduces computational burden via randomized block-coordinate implementation of an augmented projected primal-dual controller.
AI.motivation: To address secondary frequency control in transmission networks under two-way communication delays at the cyber-physical interface and limited per-update computation at the control center.
AI.method: A passivity-based control framework using an augmented projected primal-dual controller; two-way delays modeled as scattering-based passive channels; randomized block-coordinate implementation to reduce computational burden; multivariable wave-domain interface filter for additional dissipation.
AI.result: The closed-loop system preserves the target equilibrium, achieves local mean-square geometric convergence under suitable conditions, and simulations on the IEEE 14-bus system show accurate delayed closed-loop behavior with reduced per-update computational cost.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively handles communication delays and computational constraints while maintaining stability and convergence properties for secondary frequency control.

title: Lure-and-Reveal: An Exposure Framework for Stealthy Deception Attack in Multi-sensor Uncertain Systems
summary: Multi-sensor integration via error-state Kalman filter (KF) is widely employed for precise state estimation in cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, this integration exposes the system to stealthy deception attacks that render conventional detection mechanisms ineffective. We propose an exposure framework to actively reveal such stealthy attacks without modifying sensor interfaces. The framework introduces a suspect mode in which the defender injects random exposure shakes into the nominal control inputs, thus creating a discrepancy between the defender's true state estimates and the attacker's manipulated state estimates, preventing the attack from remaining stealthy. We further derive an explicit exposure condition that characterizes the minimum shake magnitude to guarantee the finite-time exposure and a compensable condition that ensures the shakes do not degrade closed-loop performance. Simulation results based on a GNSS/INS-integrated UAV system verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a framework to expose stealthy deception attacks on multi-sensor CPSs by injecting random "exposure shakes" into control inputs, creating a discrepancy between defender and attacker estimates, with conditions for guaranteed exposure and performance compensation.
AI.motivation: Multi-sensor integration via error-state KF is vulnerable to stealthy deception attacks that bypass conventional detection, necessitating a proactive defense mechanism that reveals such attacks without altering sensor interfaces.
AI.method: A suspect mode is introduced where the defender injects random exposure shakes into nominal control inputs, causing divergence between the defender's true state estimates and the attacker's manipulated estimates. The framework derives explicit exposure condition (minimum shake magnitude for finite-time exposure) and a compensable condition (to prevent performance degradation).
AI.result: Simulation on a GNSS/INS-integrated UAV system validates the framework's effectiveness in exposing stealthy attacks while maintaining closed-loop performance.
AI.conclusion: The proposed active exposure framework can reliably reveal stealthy deception attacks in multi-sensor CPSs with provable guarantees on both attack exposure and nominal performance preservation.

title: Transmission Topology Optimization using accelerated MapElites
summary: Transmission Topology Optimization has great potential to improve efficiency and flexibility of grid operations through non-costly switching actions, but previous approaches struggle with runtime performance and scalability. In this work, we present an optimization approach that leverages GPU acceleration to speed up computations. In a genetic algorithm setting, topologies are randomly mutated and evaluated in parallel for multiple optimization criteria. Combined with a fully GPU-native DC loadflow solver, there is no CPU-GPU data transfer required in the DC optimization loop. Using a variant of the illumination algorithm MapElites, we efficiently generate a set of diverse candidate solutions on the pareto front. Together with an importing and AC validation step, we present an end-to-end optimization solution that runs in under 15 minutes. The approach is currently under evaluation by operational planning operators in two European TSOs. We furthermore open-source our code at github.com/eliagroup/ToOp.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a GPU-accelerated genetic algorithm using MapElites illumination for transmission topology optimization, achieving end-to-end optimization in under 15 minutes with fully GPU-native DC loadflow and no CPU-GPU data transfer, currently being evaluated by two European TSOs with open-source code available.
AI.motivation: Transmission Topology Optimization can improve grid efficiency and flexibility via non-costly switching actions, but existing approaches suffer from poor runtime performance and scalability.
AI.method: GPU-accelerated genetic algorithm with random topology mutation and parallel multi-criteria evaluation; uses a fully GPU-native DC loadflow solver eliminating CPU-GPU data transfer; employs MapElites illumination variant to generate diverse Pareto-front solutions; includes an importing and AC validation step for end-to-end pipeline.
AI.result: End-to-end optimization completes in under 15 minutes; approach is under evaluation by operational planning operators at two European TSOs.
AI.conclusion: GPU acceleration combined with MapElites enables practical runtime for transmission topology optimization, making it feasible for real operational planning; code is open-sourced for broader use.

title: Online Learning-Based Control with Guaranteed Error Bounds for a Class of Nonlinear Systems
comment: Accepted at IFAC 2026 (23rd IFAC World Congress, Busan, Korea)
summary: In this paper, we present a learning-based control for a class of nonlinear systems that guarantees exponential stability as well as bounded output errors. The control is based on the Gaussian Process Submodel Online Learning (GPSOL) algorithm and the Disturbance Error Rate Limiting (DERL) algorithm, both of which were developed in previous work. The GPSOL algorithm provides a method to learn Gaussian Process (GP) models for subsystems online, whereas the DERL algorithm allows to limit the rate of the prediction error of these GP models. The focus of this paper is the utilization of the GP model within an adaptive controller and the derivation of corresponding stability conditions and system peak-to-peak gains by means of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). These peak-to-peak gains are then used to prescribe a desired prediction error rate for the DERL algorithm to achieve user-defined output error bounds. The gains and the related bounds were successfully verified using a simulation model. Furthermore, results form a successful experimental validation of the bounds and the overall control structure on a pneumatic test rig are presented. While the control scheme and error bounds proposed in this paper are limited to first-order single-input-single-output systems, an extension to certain classes of higher-order and multiple-input-multiple-output systems is expected to be forthcoming.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a learning-based control for nonlinear systems using GPSOL and DERL algorithms, guaranteeing exponential stability and bounded output errors. Stability conditions and peak-to-peak gains are derived via LMIs, validated through simulation and experimental testing on a pneumatic rig, though currently limited to first-order SISO systems.
AI.motivation: To achieve guaranteed exponential stability and bounded output errors in nonlinear systems by leveraging online learning of Gaussian Process models within an adaptive control framework.
AI.method: Combines GPSOL (online GP model learning for subsystems) with DERL (prediction error rate limiting). Stability conditions and peak-to-peak gains are derived via Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs), which prescribe the desired prediction error rate for DERL to meet user-defined output error bounds.
AI.result: Peak-to-peak gains and error bounds were successfully verified via simulation and experimentally validated on a pneumatic test rig.
AI.conclusion: The control scheme and error bounds are limited to first-order SISO systems, but extension to higher-order and MIMO systems is expected in future work.

title: Hierarchical 2-degree-of-freedom control combining Youla-Kucera parameterization and model predictive control
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, accepted for Europan Control Conference 2026 (ECC 2026)
summary: A hierarchical 2DOF (2-degree-of-freedom) structure combining Youla-Kucera (YK) parameterization and model predictive control (MPC) is presented in this paper. The YK parameterization employs the coprime factorization of the nominal system and controller, thereby introducing an auxiliary feedforward channel dedicated to system optimization and a controller parameterization channel. The feedforward channel is utilized to implement cascaded MPC for system optimization. The controller parameterization channel is utilized to achieve offset-free MPC by designing an appropriate YK parameter through the H2 optimal controller design.

AI.tldr: A hierarchical 2DOF control structure integrating Youla-Kucera parameterization with MPC is proposed, using coprime factorization to create feedforward (for cascaded MPC optimization) and controller parameterization (for H2 optimal offset-free MPC) channels.
AI.motivation: To combine YK parameterization with MPC to achieve both system optimization and offset-free control within a unified hierarchical 2DOF framework.
AI.method: A 2DOF structure based on YK parameterization using coprime factorization, with a feedforward channel for cascaded MPC optimization and a controller parameterization channel for H2 optimal controller design.
AI.result: The proposed structure enables cascaded MPC for optimization via the feedforward channel and offset-free MPC via the controller parameterization channel using YK parameter design.
AI.conclusion: The YK parameterization-based 2DOF framework effectively integrates MPC optimization and offset-free control through separate channels.

title: Priority-Driven Control and Communication in Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems via Reinforcement Learning
comment: Accepted to the 23rd IFAC World Congress
summary: Event-triggered control provides a mechanism for avoiding excessive use of constrained communication bandwidth in networked multi-agent systems. However, most existing methods rely on accurate system models, which may be unavailable in practice. In this work, we propose a model-free, priority-driven reinforcement learning algorithm that learns communication priorities and control policies jointly from data in decentralized multi-agent systems. By learning communication priorities, we circumvent the hybrid action space typical in event-triggered control with binary communication decisions. We evaluate our algorithm on benchmark tasks and demonstrate that it outperforms the baseline method.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a model-free, priority-driven reinforcement learning algorithm for event-triggered control in decentralized multi-agent systems, which jointly learns communication priorities and control policies from data without requiring accurate system models, outperforming baseline methods on benchmark tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing event-triggered control methods rely on accurate system models, which are often unavailable in practice, creating a need for a model-free approach.
AI.method: A model-free, priority-driven reinforcement learning algorithm that jointly learns communication priorities and control policies, circumventing the hybrid action space typical in event-triggered control with binary communication decisions.
AI.result: The algorithm outperforms baseline methods on benchmark tasks.
AI.conclusion: Model-free, priority-driven reinforcement learning is effective for event-triggered control in decentralized multi-agent systems, avoiding reliance on accurate system models.

title: Observing the state of networks with directed higher-order interactions
summary: We consider the problem of reconstructing the state of a network of nonlinear dynamical systems in the presence of directed higher-order interactions. Grounded on analytical convergence results, we propose an algorithmic observer design procedure that simultaneously selects the nodes to be measured and the observer gains. We complement the theoretical analysis with an exhaustive numerical investigation campaign that showcases the performance and robustness of the designed observer. Finally, the algorithmic procedure is used to fully reconstruct the opinions of a group of agents.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an algorithmic observer design for reconstructing the state of nonlinear dynamical networks with directed higher-order interactions, based on analytical convergence results, and demonstrates its performance through numerical experiments and opinion reconstruction in multi-agent systems.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of state reconstruction in nonlinear dynamical networks exhibiting higher-order interactions, which are prevalent in complex systems but understudied in observer design.
AI.method: An algorithmic observer design procedure grounded in analytical convergence results, which simultaneously selects measurement nodes and observer gains.
AI.result: Exhaustive numerical investigation confirms the performance and robustness of the designed observer; the method successfully reconstructs opinions in a multi-agent group.
AI.conclusion: The proposed algorithmic observer effectively reconstructs network states under directed higher-order interactions, with validated robustness and practical applicability.

title: Glycemic Safety Tube: A Provably Safe Control Framework for Artificial Pancreas Systems under Parametric Uncertainty
