summary: Type 1 diabetes eliminates the body's ability to produce insulin, making glucose regulation entirely dependent on external insulin delivery and the control algorithm. Existing closed-loop methods either rely on accurate patient-specific models or do not provide formal safety guarantees, and are often computationally demanding for wearable devices. This paper proposes Glycemic Safety Tube Control (GSTC), a model-free and computationally efficient control framework for automated insulin delivery. The method enforces clinically relevant safety bounds on glucose levels by design, ensuring that glucose remains within a prescribed safe range. We also derive feasibility conditions that guarantee safety and input constraint satisfaction under bounded meal disturbances and estimation errors. The performance of GSTC is evaluated against state-of-the-art methods, including linear and nonlinear model predictive control and sliding mode control. The results demonstrate that GSTC maintains safety under varying meal patterns and patient conditions, highlighting its robustness and computational efficiency. Overall, GSTC provides a safe, efficient, and patient-independent approach for next-generation artificial pancreas systems.

AI.tldr: Glycemic Safety Tube Control (GSTC) is a model-free, computationally efficient insulin delivery framework that enforces formal safety bounds on glucose levels without relying on patient-specific models, demonstrating robustness and efficiency against state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Type 1 diabetes requires automated insulin delivery, but existing closed-loop methods either need accurate patient models, lack formal safety guarantees, or are too computationally demanding for wearable devices.
AI.method: The paper proposes GSTC, a model-free control framework that enforces clinically relevant safety bounds on glucose levels by design, with derived feasibility conditions guaranteeing safety and input constraint satisfaction under bounded meal disturbances and estimation errors.
AI.result: GSTC maintains safety under varying meal patterns and patient conditions, outperforming or matching linear and nonlinear model predictive control and sliding mode control while being computationally efficient.
AI.conclusion: GSTC provides a safe, efficient, and patient-independent approach suitable for next-generation artificial pancreas systems, addressing key limitations of existing methods.

title: Equivariant Observer Design on SL(3) for Image Intensity-Based Homography Estimation
comment: 16 pages, 4 figures, preprint submitted to Automatica
summary: This paper addresses the problem of homography estimation using a nonlinear observer designed on the Lie group $\mathbf{SL}(3)$ that exploits the full image information through direct image registration. Unlike traditional feature-based methods, which rely on extensive feature extraction and matching, the proposed approach formulates an observer that minimises a cost function defined directly in terms of image pixel intensities. Explicit conditions ensuring the non-degeneracy of the cost function are derived, and a comprehensive analysis is conducted to characterise and generate degenerate (unobservable) image configurations. Theoretical results demonstrate local exponential convergence of the observer. To improve local convergence properties, a second-order observer variant is introduced by incorporating the Hessian of the cost function into the correction term. Simulation results demonstrate the performance of the proposed solutions on real images.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a nonlinear observer on the Lie group SL(3) for homography estimation using direct image registration (pixel intensities) instead of feature-based methods, with theoretical proofs of local exponential convergence and a second-order variant using Hessian information.
AI.motivation: Traditional feature-based homography estimation methods rely on extensive feature extraction and matching, which can be computationally expensive and error-prone. The authors aim to develop a direct method that uses full image information through pixel intensities to avoid these limitations.
AI.method: A nonlinear observer is designed on the Lie group SL(3) that minimizes a cost function defined directly in terms of image pixel intensities (direct image registration). Explicit non-degeneracy conditions are derived, and degenerate image configurations are characterized. A second-order observer variant incorporating the Hessian of the cost function is also introduced to improve local convergence.
AI.result: Theoretical results prove local exponential convergence of the observer. Simulation results on real images demonstrate the performance of both the first-order and second-order observer variants.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Lie group SL(3)-based nonlinear observer with direct image registration offers a viable alternative to feature-based homography estimation, with guaranteed local exponential convergence and improved performance via the second-order variant.
